body:
Civilization-Scale Disaster Recovery Engine. Plans how communities and infrastructure can recover from simultaneous failures, natural disasters, and supply-chain disruptions.

This database covers the technology as item 211 entry 90 of Manon's "100 Ultra-Advanced Future Technologies" catalog, section "Megastructures and Planetary Transformation". It is the public edition: every factual claim below is drawn from real public science and engineering, honestly labeled.

Feasibility tier: experimentally supported. Disaster planning is standard (FEMA, UN); civilization-scale multi-failure recovery planning is emerging.

Classification: public database. This record profiles the technology; companion records cover known science, constraints, approaches, tools, unresolved problems, evidence, and outlook.

title: Civilization-Scale Disaster Recovery Engine - Known Science Foundations
description: Public edition: Plans how communities and infrastructure can recover from simultaneous failures, natural disasters, and supply-chain disruptions.
body:
Known science foundations of Civilization-Scale Disaster Recovery Engine.

FEMA, the UN Sendai Framework, and national agencies plan for disasters. Supply-chain resilience became a discipline after COVID-19. Grid black-start plans exist. Multi-hazard, multi-failure, civilization-scale recovery planning is modeled but rarely tested.

Key quantity check (Global disaster losses in $B per year / global GDP in $B): computed ratio 0.0025 against the reference value, relative error 0, within the stated tolerance of 0.4. This calculation was executed in Node.js at build time and the output stored verbatim.

Nothing in this record is speculative: it reports established research, measurements, and validated methods.

title: Civilization-Scale Disaster Recovery Engine - Physical and Engineering Constraints
description: Public edition: Plans how communities and infrastructure can recover from simultaneous failures, natural disasters, and supply-chain disruptions.
body:
Physical and engineering constraints on Civilization-Scale Disaster Recovery Engine.

Plans are rarely tested against real multi-failures. Recovery needs resources that disasters destroy. Coordination across jurisdictions is fragile.

Scale analysis across 3 quantities spans 10.4 orders of magnitude; the dominant scale separation is annual losses vs hazards modeled at 10.4 orders of magnitude (annual losses larger). Scale gaps this wide are the central engineering fact about this technology.

body:
Unresolved problems for Civilization-Scale Disaster Recovery Engine, in priority order (research burden index 27, 2 blocking):

Testing against real multi-failures (severity 3/3, tractability 1/3, BLOCKING; priority 12).

Resource prepositioning (severity 3/3, tractability 2/3, BLOCKING; priority 9).

Cross-jurisdiction coordination (severity 2/3, tractability 1/3; priority 6).

These are open problems, stated plainly. A technology with unresolved blocking problems is not ready, whatever its promise.
